inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: FY2025 annual report and H1 2026 interim disclose no share-based payment expense and no share option scheme; basic EPS = diluted EPS (interim note 7(b)). SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,902,036,000 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim note 17(b)); no dilutive instruments, basic = diluted. Held flat: SBC is zero and there is no announced issuance.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (functional currency, confirmed in every annual report); HKEX quote in HKD. USD/HKD 7.8475 from Yahoo HKD=X at 2026-10-16T07:03Z (HKD peg band 7.75-7.85, so the rate is stable). Per-share values computed in USD then multiplied by 7.8475 for the HKD quote basis; no dual listing exists for a parity check, but the interim's own HK$0.087154 = US¢1.1113 conversion (7.8426) ties to within 0.1%.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 (FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025) so that the base revenue, the FY0 margins and the 30 June 2026 balance sheet are the same vintage. Year 1 is therefore the twelve months to June 2027. Using the Dec-2025 balance sheet against FY2026 flows, or the Jun-2026 balance sheet against FY2026 flows, would double-count or omit H1 2026 cash generation (+US$540m). TTM: revenue 3,929.6; operating EBITDA ex interest income ~1,332 (33.9%); D&A 203.9; attributable NI 574.6; NI incl NCI 834.7; OCF 1,455.6; capex 242.5.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = TTM reported FCF 1,213.1 - SBC 0 - interest income 47.2 = 1,165.9. This TTM figure is NOT a base for projection: H1 2026 OCF (1,042.8) was flattered by ~US$450m of timing items (income tax payable +166, other payables +255, contract liabilities +30) and includes the full 100% consolidated flow before the ~30% NCI leakage. Year-1 attributable owner FCF is built from components (~US$620m in base).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year UST ~4.2% + ERP 5.0% x beta 1.3 (copper, EM-listed) = 10.7%, rounded to 11.0% to reflect the Zambia/DRC/Kazakhstan jurisdiction mix and SOE governance at the discount-rate level. The group has no net debt (borrowings US$10.6m vs cash US$2.0bn) so WACC = cost of equity. Risk is charged once: the same 11.0% applies to all three scenarios; commodity-cycle, regulatory (DRC quota) and operational risks live in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: TTM lease cash (principal + interest, cash-flow statement) = 3.763+0.903 + 7.095+2.371 - 1.736-0.654 = US$11.7m = 0.30% of revenue, charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (US$63.8m non-current + 12.0m current at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (TTM ROU depreciation ~US$6m) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. NCI (ZCCM-IH 15%/20% in NFCA/Luanshya, Yunnan Copper 40% in CCS, Huachin SARL 32.5-37.5% in the DRC leach plants, GCM 45% in Kambove, YH Metal 43% in Lualaba smelter) takes a stable ~30% of consolidated profit (FY2021-H1 2026: 69-73% attributable). cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED tax + NCI leakage rate on EBIT: income tax ~29% of pre-tax profit x NCI ~30.5% of after-tax = 1 - 0.71 x 0.695 = 50.7%; set at 51%. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT ex interest income 774.6 x 0.49 = 380 vs attributable NI ex after-leakage interest ~381; TTM 1,128 x 0.49 = 553 vs ~546. Net reinvestment (capex - D&A) is charged at 100% rather than 70%, which is slightly conservative. The NCI balance sheet stock (US$1,115.6m) is NOT deducted in the bridge (that would charge it twice), but NCI's share of subsidiary-held cash is (see equity_bridge).
inputs.interest_income_note: Net cash (~US$2.0bn) is ~3x the FCF base, so TTM interest income of US$47.2m is stripped from the flows and the matching assets (cash and the US$346.2m deposits with a fellow subsidiary) are carried in the bridge at book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations file applied: dual currency (USD flows / HKD quote), USD-built WACC, treatment-B leases, NCI folded into a combined leakage rate, stripped interest income with matching assets in the bridge, SBC-zero (band collapses, band_position null). THROUGH-CYCLE FRAMING: CNMC is a price-taking copper miner-smelter (~550kt copper output, ~143kt from owned mines; ~60% of volume is purchased concentrate at ~12% margin, owned-mine copper and tolling carry the margin). The latest period sits at a cycle peak: LME copper averaged US$13,088/t in H1 2026 (+39% YoY) and COMEX trades at ~US$14,600/t on the valuation date versus ~US$9.6k in FY2025 and US$8-9.5k in FY2021-24; H1 2026 operating EBITDA margin was 43.7% against a FY2021-25 average of ~24%. The base case therefore does NOT capitalise the current margin: revenue and margin are held near spot for year 1 (H2 2026 is largely locked in) and normalised to a US$10.5k/t mid-cycle price and a 28% EBITDA margin by year 3-4, with volume growth from Luanshya New Mine, Chambishi SE Phase II, Kambove MSESA, Samba and the 70%-owned Benkala (Kazakhstan, ~45ktpa) project layered on top. Cobalt is carried at zero in base (production suspended March 2026 after no DRC export-quota allocation; it was 0.0% of FY2025 revenue). Terminal cap multiples are cyclical-grade (base 12x, bull 14x, bear 10x). Dividend policy (~40% payout) does not affect the valuation but the US$205.1m paid/declared since the 30 June balance sheet is deducted in the bridge.

equity_bridge.item: Deposits with a fellow subsidiary (CNMC Group finance company), 30 Jun 2026
equity_bridge.note: Interim note 12(iv): interest-bearing related-party deposits, cash-like; interest on them is inside the stripped interest income, so the asset goes into the bridge (matching-asset rule). Counterparty is the SASAC-owned parent group; carried at book, no haircut.

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend (US cents 4.1446, US$161.7m) unpaid at 30 Jun 2026, paid Jul-2026
equity_bridge.note: Interim note 17(a): declared in H1 2026, no 'dividends paid to shareholders' line in H1 financing activities, so it sits in the 30 June cash and payables. A buyer today does not receive it.

equity_bridge.item: H1 2026 interim dividend (US cents 1.1113, US$43.4m) paid 17 Sep 2026
equity_bridge.note: Declared 21 Aug 2026 out of H1 2026 earnings, which are inside the 30 June cash balance; paid after the balance date and before the valuation date.

equity_bridge.item: NCI share of cash held in non-wholly-owned operating subsidiaries (estimate)
equity_bridge.note: Holding-company ('unallocated') interest income was US$9.1m of US$15.8m group interest income in H1 2025 (~57%), implying ~43% of group cash sits in the 55-85%-owned Zambian/DRC subsidiaries; at a ~30% blended NCI share that is ~US$270m, rounded to US$300m to cover CNMHK's own minority. Company-level cash was US$430.5m plus ~US$300m of loans to subsidiaries at 31 Dec 2025 (AR note 36). Without this deduction, attributable-only flows plus 100% of group cash would hand shareholders cash that belongs to ZCCM-IH, Yunnan Copper, Huachin, GCM and YH Metal.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle volume growth (~1.5-3% from brownfield projects and Benkala) plus ~2.5% USD inflation; the 17.5% equity CAGR is retained peak-cycle earnings and is not a forward revenue proxy for a price-taker
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 17.5% diverges by >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 5.7%: book value compounded on rising copper prices and a ~60% retention ratio while revenue was flat-to-down on volume mix (less self-produced blister sold, more tolling). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-3.3%) is below reported (-1.7%) only because interest income on the growing cash pile is stripped; SBC is zero.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), USD millions, calendar fiscal years. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (0) - interest income: FY2020 263.7, FY2022 726.9, FY2025 657.1. FY2022 was a working-capital-release year (capex only US$50m), which depresses the 3yr FCF CAGRs.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (to Jun-2027): H2 2026 at ~US$14k/t LME with volumes on the FY2026 plan, H1 2027 easing toward US$12k -> ~US$4.6bn (+17% on TTM 3.93bn). Y2-Y3: price normalises to a US$10.5k/t mid-cycle, partly offset by ~3%/yr volume. Y4-Y7: +4.5% = 2.5% USD inflation + ~2% volume as Luanshya New Mine, Chambishi SE Phase II, Samba and Benkala (first concentrate ~2029-30) ramp. Y8-Y10: +3%.
base.margin_rationale: Operating EBITDA ex interest income: H1 2026 43.7%, FY2025 27.9%, FY2021-25 average ~24% at US$8-9.6k copper. 41% Y1 (H2 2026 near spot, H1 2027 lower), 33% Y2, then 28% at mid-cycle: FY2025's level plus the mix shift to tolling/cathodes and sulphuric acid, net of Zambian sliding-scale royalty and power-cost inflation.
base.capex_rationale: TTM capex 6.2% of revenue (US$242m). Pipeline: Samba US$276m, Mwambashi-B US$112m, Kambove West Ph I US$86m, Chambishi SE Ph II TBM, Benkala construction -> ~US$385m/yr (9%) in Y2-Y3, fading to 7% (sustaining + modest growth, vs D&A 6.5%).
base.wc_rationale: Miner/smelter with receivables (US$408m, provisional pricing), inventory (US$662m) and input-VAT receivables (US$142m) exceeding payables: growth consumes ~10% of the revenue increase; revenue declines in Y2-Y3 release cash.
base.tax_rationale: Combined cash tax (~29% of pre-tax; Zambia/DRC 30% statutory, cash tax paid tracks expense over 3 years) plus ~30.5% NCI share of after-tax profit = 51% leakage on EBIT, held flat: NCI percentages are fixed by shareholder agreements and no change in Zambian/DRC corporate tax is assumed (royalty is in COGS).
base.terminal_rationale: 12x cap on a cyclical: Gordon at 11%/2.5% is 12.1x so the cap and Gordon coincide; the terminal year is a mid-cycle year, not a peak.

bull.rationale: Structural copper deficit from 2027 (grid, EV, AI data-centre demand against constrained mine supply) keeps LME at US$13-14k/t nominal; margins settle at 34% rather than 28%; brownfield projects and Benkala deliver ~2-3% volume growth on top of inflation; cobalt exports resume on a 2027 quota allocation (upside not separately modelled); SML stays rehabilitated and Zambian power is contracted. Cap 14x reflects a sector re-rating in a deficit market.

bear.rationale: Copper mean-reverts hard: supply response plus a China/global industrial slowdown takes LME to US$8.5-9k/t by 2027 (the FY2021-24 range); Zambia's hydropower deficit and diesel back-up push unit costs up while the sliding royalty gives no relief on the way down; the DRC cobalt quota is never restored and the quota logic spreads to copper export permits; project capex continues (TBM, Samba, Benkala) into a weaker price, so capex stays above D&A; margins revert to the FY2020-23 band (~21%). Cap 10x: the market pays a trough multiple for an African SOE-controlled miner.

scenario_narratives.base: A through-cycle valuation at a cycle peak. H2 2026 is largely locked in near spot (LME ~US$14k/t, FY2026 volume targets on track: 56% of cathode and 52-53% of blister/anode and mine-copper targets achieved in H1), so year 1 carries a 41% operating EBITDA margin on ~US$4.6bn revenue. From there copper normalises to a US$10.5k/t mid-cycle over two years and the margin settles at 28%, FY2025's level plus the mix shift toward higher-margin tolling (55.9% margin), copper cathodes and sulphuric acid. Volume grows ~2-3% a year from Luanshya New Mine, Chambishi SE Phase II (TBM trial excavation began April 2026), Kambove MSESA, Samba and, from ~2029-30, the 70%-owned Benkala project. Cobalt is zero throughout (suspended since March 2026 on the DRC quota miss). Tax and the ~30% NCI leakage are charged in the flows at a combined 51% of EBIT; the group's US$2.0bn cash is added net of US$205m of dividends already paid, plus US$346m of deposits with the parent's finance company, less a ~US$300m estimate of the minorities' share of subsidiary cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural-deficit thesis holds: constrained mine supply against grid, EV and AI data-centre demand keeps LME copper at US$13-14k/t nominal through the decade, so the current 43% margin only fades to 34% as costs inflate and royalties step up. Brownfield projects and Benkala add ~2-3% volume a year on top of inflation, tolling volumes keep rising as the Zambian/DRC concentrate market tightens, SML remains stable, Zambian power is secured under contract, and cobalt exports resume under a 2027 ARECOMS allocation (not separately modelled, so this case is still conservative on cobalt). The market pays a 14x terminal multiple for a net-cash, 40%-payout copper producer inside the MSCI China Index.
scenario_narratives.bear: Copper mean-reverts and the jurisdictions bite. A supply response and a global industrial slowdown take LME back to US$8.5-9k/t by 2027, the range of FY2021-24; revenue falls ~25% from the year-1 level and margins revert to the ~21% FY2020-23 band because the sliding Zambian royalty gives nothing back on the way down while diesel back-up for the hydropower deficit (707MW short in 2025 and widening) lifts unit costs. The DRC cobalt quota is never restored and permit-style controls spread to copper; SML or Lualaba suffer further suspensions. Capex for the TBM, Samba and Benkala continues into the downturn, so free cash flow is thin, and the market applies a 10x trough multiple to a SASAC-controlled African miner.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; bear is raised to 25% because the company is a price-taker being valued at a record copper price, has already lost a product line to a single regulator's decision (DRC cobalt quota, March 2026), runs in a power-deficit grid, and is SOE-controlled. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold: copper staying above US$13k/t for a decade AND the brownfield/Benkala pipeline delivering on time in Zambia, the DRC and Kazakhstan.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on attributable flows for a cyclical copper miner-smelter valued at a cycle peak. The flows are normalised to a US$10.5k/t copper price and a 28% EBITDA margin rather than capitalising the H1 2026 43.7% margin; the ~30% minority leakage and the ~29% cash tax are charged in the flows at a combined 51% of EBIT; interest income is stripped and the US$2.0bn cash, the US$346m related-party deposits and the dividends already paid are bridged explicitly, with an estimated US$300m of subsidiary cash reserved for the minorities. The USD valuation is converted to the HKD quote at 7.8475. Terminal multiples are capped at cyclical levels (10x/12x/14x).
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper price: every US$1,000/t on ~143kt of owned-mine copper plus the margin on ~400kt of processed concentrate is worth roughly US$150-200m of EBITDA, so the mid-cycle price assumption (US$10.5k/t base) drives most of the gap between the scenarios.

The NCI cash estimate (US$300m) is derived from the interest-income split, not disclosed; if most group cash sits at the holding companies the deduction is too large by up to ~US$0.05/share (HK$0.4), and vice versa.

Combined 51% leakage assumes NCI stays ~30% of profit; a shift of profit toward the 85%-owned NFCA (Chambishi SE Phase II) lowers leakage, a shift toward the 55-57%-owned DRC smelter/Kambove raises it.
Zambian fiscal regime (sliding royalty up to 10% at current prices, periodic rewrites) and DRC export-quota policy can move margins by several points with no notice.
Power: Zambia's hydropower deficit forces diesel generation and production stoppages; a multi-year dry cycle would push the base margin toward the bear path.
Related-party deposits (US$346m with the CNMC Group finance company) and the acquisition of Benkala from a related party are captive-capital exposures carried at book.

Deposits, timing of tax payable (US$362m at 30 June) and provisional-pricing receivables/payables make reported FCF swing by hundreds of millions between halves; the component build ignores these timing effects.
